cse-2000-a-2-2.approach: Write the union rule with independence, $\Pr(E_1\cup E_2)=2p-p^2$, set it to 1 and solve for $p$.

steps.title: Union with independence
steps.body:
Let $p=\Pr(E_1)=\Pr(E_2)$. Independence gives $\Pr(E_1\cap E_2)=p\cdot p=p^2$, so
$$\Pr(E_1\cup E_2)=p+p-p^2=2p-p^2.$$

steps.title: Solve
steps.body: $$2p-p^2=1 \;\Rightarrow\; p^2-2p+1=0 \;\Rightarrow\; (p-1)^2=0 \;\Rightarrow\; p=1.$$

$p=\tfrac14$ gives $2\cdot\tfrac14-\tfrac1{16}=\tfrac7{16}\ne1$.
$p=\tfrac12$ gives $1-\tfrac14=\tfrac34\ne1$.
$p=1$ gives $2-1=1$ — the only root of $(p-1)^2=0$.
